text: maria: 🔔 Escalation from ACME. After we flipped their egress proxy yesterday their Private deployment started getting intermittent 403s when trying to decrypt model keys via KMS. Customer says it started ~22:10 UTC. Sample from runtime logs attached below. maria: ``` 2026-02-09T22:12:03Z ERROR runtime.kms: decrypt failed status=403 body=SignatureDoesNotMatch requestId=abcd-1234 stack: com.redwood.kms.KmsClientException: 403 ``` sanjay: thx. do we have customer id and region? sound like sigv4 mismatch or proxy mutating headers. maria: ACME (acct-84321), region us-east-1. They use our Private package with an outbound proxy (squid) on their edge, which they rolled to a new image yesterday. dmitri: quick repro from a bastion will help. can someone run a curl from their env to the KMS endpoint (use the proxy) and paste the raw response? specifically: `curl -v -x http://10.0.3.5:3128 https://kms.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/` maria: ran it, pasted output:``` * Connected to 10.0.3.5 (10.0.3.5) port 3128 (#0) > GET https://kms.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/ HTTP/1.1 > Host: kms.us-east-1.amazonaws.com > User-Agent: curl/7.79.1 > Accept: */* > < HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden < Content-Type: application/xml < Content-Length: 236 < Sender SignatureDoesNotMatch The request signature we calculated does not match the signature you provided. ``` emily: that exact error is consistent with header rewriting (date/host/authorization) or an http-proxy stripping x-amz-* headers before forwarding. if the proxy is terminating TLS and reissuing to the target, it can also change the Host header. both will break SigV4. sanjay: ops-bot — did the recent squid image change include any header-strip config? ops-bot: deploy-log: squid-image:v2.1.7 -> v2.2.0 rolled 2026-02-09T21:45Z; changed config: `headers_to_strip = ["via", "x-forwarded-for", "user-agent"]` (released note: remove sensitive headers). dmitri: bingo. that config will strip all x-* headers if misconfigured pattern matches. mitigation options: 1) revert proxy change 2) add an allowlist to preserve x-amz-* and Authorization headers 3) create a VPC interface endpoint for KMS (com.amazonaws.us-east-1.kms) so traffic doesn't rely on that proxy, or 4) allow direct egress to KMS and disable proxy for our control-plane subnets. emily: for short-term we should advise ACME to preserve aws headers. sample squid config snippet to keep them: `request_header_access Authorization allow all` and `request_header_access x-amz-* allow all` (verify exact directive for their proxy). maria: i've requested ACME ops to revert or patch to preserve x-amz-* and auth headers. also told them about the VPC endpoint option. sending them the curl output and squid diff. dmitri: security review note: if teams plan to use a shared egress proxy, we need a design doc that lists headers that must be preserved (Authorization, x-amz-*, x-redwood-*). add to Private deployment runbook. emily: i'll file a short RFC and a runbook PR. tagging network and infra. maria: ack. I'll keep this thread updated once ACME confirms patch/rollback. thanks all :thumbsup:
